applies_to.launch: copilot -p <task> --output-format json --stream on (standard output) and the native session directory's events.jsonl
applies_to.selection: the version the capture discovered with copilot --version before and after the run (neither route reports it on every record; the session file's session.start reports copilotVersion)

executor: journal-ocsf-writer CopilotEventsMapper with CopilotTools and CopilotAccounting (direct Java); one record at a time
identity: copilot.events.identity.v1: id is the event's own id, kept by a persisted event on both routes; data.apiCallId (assistant message, usage record) is the provider call id of a model response (response_uid); data.toolCallId is the model-facing tool call id (tool_call_uid, identity_basis 1) on the request, start and completion; data.messageId is the CLI's message id (item_uid); data.interactionId is the user interaction (turn_uid). A session is reported only by session.start (data.sessionId) and result (sessionId); no other event is given a session another source reports

family_kind_table.meaning: a built-in tool's documented name selects its kind (view reads a file or directory, bash executes a command, edit and create change files, grep and glob search); every other name is 99 other

namespace_kind_bindings.meaning: an MCP tool (data.mcpServerName, data.mcpToolName) takes a kind only from a reviewed binding of that exact server and tool; none is declared, so every MCP tool is 99 other

rules.owner: session_uid = data.sessionId; settings = data (copilotVersion, producer, context)
turn_uid = data.interactionId; one text block from data.content; transformedContent kept in data
one text block from data.content (the system message as recorded)
response_uid = data.apiCallId; item_uid = data.messageId; text block from data.content when non-empty
tool_call_uid = toolRequests[].toolCallId; tool_name, arguments as requested; response_uid = data.apiCallId
tool_call_uid = data.toolCallId; tool_name = data.toolName (the CLI's encoded name); MCP target from data.mcpServerName/mcpToolName with a CallToolRequestParams projection

status from data.success (Reported); tool_result.data = data.result; structured_result = data.result.structuredContent; data.error as a CLI-reported tool failure (layer 3); MCP CallToolResult projection {content: data.result.contents, structuredContent}

response_uid = data.usage.apiCallId; per-call usage (scope 2 Model response, final, scope total); cost_observations: data.usage.cost as quantity kind 3 Model cost multiplier, data.usage.copilotUsage.totalNanoAiu as kind 4 Nano-AIU

cumulative session usage from data.accountingSnapshot.tokenDetails (scope 5, provisional, cumulative snapshot) and per model from modelMetrics (scope 6); premium requests (kind 2) and nano-AIU (kind 4)

response_uid = data.promptCacheBreakState[0].models[lastActiveModel].model_call_id; usage = accountingSnapshot.lastCallInputTokens/lastCallOutputTokens with that entry's cache_read/cache_write (scope 2, final): the last call's full usage, the only per-call usage standard output reports
as the checkpoint, from data.accountingSnapshot, final
exit_code = exitCode; session_uid = sessionId; result.usage.premiumRequests as kind 2 at run scope

selector.type: any other (turn start/end, deltas, model-call progress, shell output, partial results, background tasks, idle)

rules.owner: retained whole with the meaning the mapper states

rules.selector: a record that is not one JSON object

rules.owner: the record retained whole with the failure

data.toolCallId identifies the call; data.partialOutput is one partial result observation. reported_state retains the native record type, status Unknown with Unavailable basis. Distinct native event ids preserve repeated partial outputs; no terminal outcome is inferred.

candidate.status: EXPERIMENTAL candidate (2026-10-24): tested on one sanitized live 1.0.100 run (copilot-otel-1) and its final assembly; not admitted: no field-disposition catalog or oracle profile yet; tested candidate behaviour is not approved support

quantity_semantics: Selected execution quantities retain their exact reported value and source path, and add the extension-defined common concept and measurement_window. Model configuration limits are capacities, never consumption. Unknown-unit quantities remain unresolved.
